messages:
lucy: Heads-up — seeing a sustained jump in per-token latency for /generate (us-west) starting ~03:12UTC. p50 OK, p95 creeping, but p99 doubled. KV cache hit ratio dropped at the same time.

omar: Do you have the profiling snippets or Prom queries?

lucy: Paste of quick PromQL and a tiny flame snippet:
```
# kv hit ratio per route (1m)
sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total{route="/generate"}[1m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total{route="/generate"}[1m]))

# token latency breakdown (per-token p99)
sum(rate(token_generation_latency_seconds_bucket{le="0.1",route="/generate"}[1m]))
```
flame: kernel int8_opt kernel_enter -> fast path fell back to slow_copy for long sequences; kernel selector logged: "selected int8_opt (seq_threshold=1024)" but observed seq_len ~ 1800 so we hit fallback. KV evictions spiked (prefix_ttl) around 03:11.

raj: If KV hit ratio dropped first, maybe a bad eviction pattern warmed by a release? Any deploys around 03:00-03:10?

lucy: No infra deploys. We did push kernel selector tweak yesterday (dynamic thresholds) that widened int8_opt eligibility. Selector logs show a few misclassifications when lookahead tokenization changed (longer prompts from some customers).

emily: Two ideas: 1) immediate mitigation: bump prefix TTL for the most impacted route to avoid cold misses and warm hot prefixes. 2) short-term revert of the dynamic selector to previous rule while we triage.

omar: Agreed on TTL bump. Also: we should tune the kernel selection to use a per-route sequence-length histogram rather than global threshold. Right now the selector uses a fixed seq_threshold=1024 which doesn't match some customer workloads.

sasha: I created a dashboard panel showing "seq length distribution by route" + overlay of kernel choice counts. We can add an alert rule: only page on p99 burn_rate > 1.5 sustained for 5m AND kv_hit_ratio < 0.6. That avoids paging on short blips.

lucy: Proposed burn rate formula I used for the alert: burn_rate = observed_p99 / slo_p99. We translate to effective SLO burn as: if burn_rate * (window_minutes/5) > 1 then escalate. For pager we require burn_rate >= 1.5 for 5m. For #alerts slack channel threshold set at 1.2 for 3m.

raj: For anomaly detection (experimental): require both statistical deviation (>2 sigma over baseline) AND absolute delta (>20ms) to reduce false positives from low-latency routes. Also only consider routes with >1000 tokens/min to avoid noise.

infra-bot: Incident created INC-2026-42; owners: @lucy, @omar; pager on-call: @sasha.

omar: Action items: (1) lucy — bump TTL for /generate prefixes and post results in 10m, (2) emily — revert selector flag in canary for 1h and monitor, (3) sasha — add seq-histogram panel and implement burn_rate alert with the 5m sustained rule, (4) raj — draft a short-term kernel-selector change to use per-route 95th pctile seq length.

lucy: I'll post kv metrics in 5m. If TTL bump doesn't help, we flip selector.

sasha: I'll also add a compact p99 token-latency breakdown per-route (kernel path, kv_miss, batching_wait) so we can attribute quickly.

omar: Thanks — let's avoid noisy pages; prefer Slack alerts at first unless burn is clearly sustained.

lucy: ack, tracking in the thread.
